newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian guards flee second crossing to Greece.
newsitem.headline: Albanian guards flee second crossing to Greece.

text.p: Albanian border guards fled the second main crossing point to Greece on Thursday at Kapshtice near the southeast town of Korce, witnesses said.
Armed rebels opened the customs and passport stations and let cars and trucks roll through unchecked.
The main Albania-Greece crossing at Kakavia has been deserted since last week and armed gangs have been demanding money from travellers at the border.
Greek television showed men and boys looting the army munitions depot outside of Korce, gleefully ripping open hundreds of crates of arms. Trucks rolled up to fill up with guns.
One group of soldiers walked away unarmed.
"The officers ran away first, then we followed," one unarmed soldier said. "We had nothing to eat but onions and cabbage".
The young conscripts said they would now walk to their homes.
People leaving Korce said the town had gone over to the rebels and that several people had been wounded in shooting. There was no independent confirmation of the reports.
If Korce has fallen to the rebels, then almost the entire south of the Balkan country of 3.4 million people would be held by anti-government forces.
Greece has increase security along its long border with Albania, fearing a wave of refugees as violence sweeps the country. Greece already has some 350,000 illegal Albanians.
